<!-- Generated by scripts/build_help.py from Puzzle's own data: don't edit. -->


F1 on a row of the Properties panel opens its entry here.

<!-- key: field:design_life -->
### Design life

How many repetitions of the duty the part must last. Damage and the safety factor are taken at it.

<!-- key: field:diameter -->
### Diameter

The round's diameter, for its size factor.

<!-- key: field:endurance_limit -->
### Endurance limit

A measured rotating-beam endurance limit S'e. Blank: 0.5 Sut, steels only (Shigley Eq. 6-8).

<!-- key: field:expression -->
### Expression

An expression over the names listed below, evaluated at each node.

<!-- key: field:extreme -->
### Extreme

Keep the largest or the smallest over the cases.

<!-- key: field:height -->
### Height

The rectangle's height h, for de = 0.808√(h·b).

<!-- key: field:life_model -->
### Life model

Where cycles to failure come from: Shigley's S-N line from the tensile strength, the material's measured S-N curve, or its strain-life model.

<!-- key: field:loading -->
### Loading

Each kind of cycle. Fully reversed: the case and its reverse (mean zero). Zero-based: the case, then nothing (amplitude and mean half of it). Range: between a range combination's case 1 and case 2. Scale multiplies the stresses; cycles count per repetition of the duty (Miner's rule sums them).

<!-- key: field:mean_stress -->
### Mean stress

The completely reversed stress as damaging as the cycle's amplitude and mean (Shigley Sec. 6-12). A compressive mean gets no benefit.

<!-- key: field:method -->
### Method

How the cases combine.

<!-- key: field:misc_factor -->
### Misc factor

Other effects kf: plating, corrosion, fretting (Shigley Sec. 6-9).

<!-- key: field:name -->
### Name

The name the tree and the results list show.

<!-- key: field:notch_factor -->
### Notch factor

Kf, multiplying the alternating stress. A modelled bolt's thread takes its own, the bolt's thread Kf (ADR 0077).

<!-- key: field:notch_from -->
### Notch from

The fatigue stress-concentration factor, given, or Kf = 1 + q(Kt − 1) with Neuber's notch sensitivity q (Shigley Eqs. 6-32 to 6-35, steels). Leave it at 1 where the mesh resolves the notch: its stresses already include Kt.

<!-- key: field:notch_kt -->
### Notch kt

The theoretical stress-concentration factor Kt, from charts or a fine model.

<!-- key: field:notch_on_mean -->
### Notch on mean

Kf on the mean stress too. Shigley applies it to the alternating stress only for ductile materials.

<!-- key: field:notch_radius -->
### Notch radius

The notch root radius r, for Neuber's √a/√r.

<!-- key: field:notch_shear -->
### Notch shear

Neuber's constant for torsion rather than bending and axial loads.

<!-- key: field:quantity -->
### Quantity

The result compared at each node across the cases.

<!-- key: field:reliability -->
### Reliability

Reliability factor ke = 1 − 0.08·za (Shigley Eq. 6-29, Table 6-5).

<!-- key: field:size -->
### Size

Size factor kb (Shigley Eqs. 6-20 to 6-25): rotating rounds, non-rotating rounds and rectangles by their effective diameter; axial loading has none.

<!-- key: field:sn_curve -->
### Sn curve

Which of the material's S-N curves to read (Material builder, Fatigue tab).

<!-- key: field:source -->
### Source

The results the equation reads: a study's latest run, or another derived result.

<!-- key: field:stress -->
### Stress

How each node's stress tensor becomes one number. Signed von Mises keeps the sign of the largest principal stress, so compression doesn't count as tension.

<!-- key: field:surface -->
### Surface

Surface factor ka = a·Sut^b (Shigley Eq. 6-19, Table 6-2).

<!-- key: field:temperature -->
### Temperature

Temperature factor kd (Shigley Eq. 6-27, 21 to 538 °C).

<!-- key: field:unit -->
### Unit

The kind of unit the value has, so it shows in the display units.

<!-- key: field:width -->
### Width

The rectangle's width b, for de = 0.808√(h·b).
